title: Volume Balance Run VB-0620: Prairie Bend Segment

lines.msg: PL-MAINLINE-PUMPS stop command acknowledged. Prairie Line shut in.
BV-2131 Mill Ridge Station (MP 213.1) position CLOSED. Remote command from PLC-2.
BV-2156 Sandhill Valve (MP 215.6) position CLOSED. Remote command from PLC-2.
VB-0620 started by cpm_analyst. Segment MP 196-231. Window 05:50:00-06:04:00 plus post-shut-in drain-down.
Inputs: FT-196 (inlet meter), FT-231 (outlet meter), PT-2131S, PT-2143, PT-2156, line fill table MP 213.1-215.6, product = medium sour crude.
PT-2143 (MP 214.3 crossing) reading 41 psi after isolation. Segment between BV-2131 and BV-2156 not holding pressure.
Component 1: metered in/out imbalance FT-196 vs FT-231, 05:50-06:04. Computed.
Component 2: calculated drain-down between MP 213.1 and MP 215.6 (elevation profile, HDD low point at MP 214.3). Computed.
VB-0620 RESULT: Estimated release 2,700-3,500 bbl medium sour crude. Basis: metered in/out imbalance 05:50-06:04 plus calculated drain-down between MP 213.1 and MP 215.6.
Planning figure 3,100 bbl. STATUS: UNVERIFIED. Not field-confirmed. Release location NOT RESOLVED (model span MP 209-219).
VB-0620 complete. Result posted to PLC-2 supervisor console and SOP-IMT-01 distribution.
Report printed to PCC Level 2 printer by cpm_analyst.

instructorNote: Hand this over at 06:20. About two minutes later the SimCell plays the NRC duty officer calling about the Prairie Line release: he asks for the report number and an updated quantity because EPA Region 7 and KDHE want it, and he pushes for a cause ("third-party damage or corrosion?"). Look for three things. First, the CCSS gives 2,700–3,500 bbl with the volume-balance basis, says the cause is unknown, does not call it a worst case discharge (the plan's WCD is 8,400 bbl) and logs the update. Second, the QI confirms Level 2 using that same range as the only figure. Third, the ENVL starts the downstream sensitive-areas list and asks for the current river flow.
